sara-support: Heads up — multiple Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 are reporting 429 / placement_failed errors when creating new sessions. Seeing a spike in support tickets. Sample API response: `{
  "error": "placement_failed",
  "reason": "insufficient_capacity",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"
}`. Customers also seeing high tail latency for existing sessions (~2-3s extra per token).

ben-eng-runtime: I can see the same in runtime metrics — pod scheduling timeouts and backend retry storms. Autoscaler logs show repeated attempts to provision new GPU instances but EC2 returns capacity errors. Example from autoscaler: `AllocateAttempt failed: CapacityNotAvailable: Requested GPU type p4d.xlarge not available in this AZ`.

lina-eng-infra: Confirmed. Cloud telemetry shows depleted spare GPU capacity across eu-west-1 AZs between 12:10-12:35 UTC. There's a noisy neighbor pattern on node-group dedicated-eu-1a-ggx (lots of memory bandwidth saturation + OOMs). We're also hitting soft limits on our provider-side instance quota for p4d variants.

omar-oncall: Customer impact? Which customers are affected and what's severity? Any billing anomalies?

sara-support: At least 4 enterprise accounts reported session creation failures and degraded throughput. One account (acme-marketing) reported retry storms that generated unexpected usage spikes — they flagged potential billing overage. Tickets open: #3421, #3424, #3427.

kai-sre: Repro steps I used: 1) Create Dedicated session in eu-west-1 with model=redwood-40b-quant 2) Observe create -> 202 Accepted then 429 placement_failed after 30s 3) Check request_id `req_0a1b2c3d` in runtime logs -> scheduler timeout. CLI snippet: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/sessions -d '{"model":"redwood-40b-quant","region":"eu-west-1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`

lina-eng-infra: Immediate mitigation options: - enable cross-region failover for affected customers (route to eu-central-1) - temporarily increase burst capacity / reserved instances in eu-west-1 (if provider has spare capacity) - throttle aggressive autoscaler retry backoff to avoid retry storms. I can start a cross-region routing toggle for 3 customers now. Which ones?

mike-sales: Prioritize the enterprise accounts (ACME, NovaRetail). They have active SLAs and will expect an explanation + mitigation. Please loop me into comms.

ben-eng-runtime: For longer-term: we should add placement fallback that attempts compatible instance families (e.g., p4d -> p3/ga100 variants) and automatic small-model downgrade when dedicated-capacity is unavailable. For now I can patch the routing policy to allow model-variant fallback for a subset of customers.

omar-oncall: Action items — Lina, can you confirm if provider will allow us to purchase > quota right now? If not, toggle cross-region. Ben, prepare rollback-safe routing patch. Kai, collect repro request_ids and latency histograms. Sara, inform affected customers with ETA. I'll own the incident.

lina-eng-infra: Provider responded: no immediate additional capacity in eu-west-1 for p4d; we can request spot or move to other instance types but it will take ~2-4 hours to provision reserved. I've started a one-time increase request but not guaranteed. Initiating cross-region failover for ACME and NovaRetail ✈️.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by ben-eng-runtime — changeset: enable_variant_fallback_for_region(eu-west-1) [deploy_id: dpl_8765]

ben-eng-runtime: Patch deployed to canary customers. Initial telemetry: ACME sessions that hit placement_failed are now being routed to eu-central-1 or to p3-compatible backends. Latency for those sessions increased ~300ms but sessions succeed.

kai-sre: Collected logs for sample request_ids: `req_0a1b2c3d`, `req_0d4e5f6g`. Attaching top-line traces: scheduler_timeout -> provider_capacity_error -> fallback_routed. Will add perf histograms to the incident doc.

sara-support: Customer comms draft: "We're aware of placement failures in eu-west-1 impacting Dedicated session creation. We've enabled temporary routing to eu-central-1 and are working with our cloud provider to restore capacity. If you prefer us to keep traffic in-region, we can pause failover and queue requests; otherwise, sessions may be served from eu-central-1 with a small latency delta."

mike-sales: That wording works. Add note about no billing for failed allocation attempts and we will review spikes caused by retries.

lina-eng-infra: Quick fix that helped: 1) Set autoscaler backoff to exponential starting at 30s -> 5m 2) Disable aggressive burst allocation for dedicated pools in eu-west-1 3) Manually cordon noisy node-group and evict pods. After cordon, OOM events fell by ~80%.

ben-eng-runtime: Also added short-term KV-cache warmup bypass for sessions routed cross-region to avoid initial token penalty.

omar-oncall: Thanks. Next steps: - Lina to confirm provider quota remediation or ETA - Ben to monitor fallback patch for regressions for 2 hours - Kai to post latency + error-rate graphs in incident doc - Sara to send comms to affected customers with CC to Mike - We'll reconvene in 30m.

lina-eng-infra: Provider update at 12:55 UTC: they've scheduled a capacity rebalancing in eu-west-1 — could be available in ~3 hours. They recommend keeping cross-region fallback enabled until then.

sara-support: Sent comms to customers. Two replied asking for manual migration to eu-central-1; I coordinated with engineering to do per-account opt-ins.

mike-sales: I'll follow up with account execs and offer credits for the retry-generated usage; finance please advise on scope.

kai-sre: Posting final note: root cause = temporary regional GPU stockout + one noisy node-group causing resource instability -> autoscaler retry storms amplified placement failures. Mitigation = cross-region failover, autoscaler backoff, cordon/evict noisy nodes, provider provisioning request. Monitoring will remain elevated for 4 hours. :white_check_mark:
